questions.q: What triggers the flow in this lab's scenario?
options: A record is deleted from the CRM
An incident is created with Priority 1 - Critical
A user manually runs the flow from a button
A Teams message is received
questions.explain: The flow triggers on Incident created with a condition of Priority is 1 - Critical.

questions.q: Why does the Teams half of the flow need no REST step configuration at all?
options: Because Teams doesn't support any kind of flow integration
Because the Teams Spoke already provides a pre-built 'Post Message' action, so it's configuration (channel, message) rather than a REST call
Because Microsoft Teams requires a Script step instead
Because only CRM integrations are allowed to use spokes
questions.explain: A spoke exists for Teams, so the lab uses its pre-built action instead of configuring a generic REST step.

questions.q: What does the generic REST step's endpoint configuration rely on in this lab?
options: A hardcoded URL and password typed directly into the REST step
A Connection & Credential Alias pointing at the CRM's API base URL
The Teams Spoke's own authentication profile
No endpoint configuration is needed for a GET request
questions.explain: The REST step's endpoint is built from a Connection & Credential Alias rather than a URL and credential hardcoded into this one flow.

questions.q: What happens to the CRM response's account_tier field in this lab?
options: It is discarded after the REST step runs
It is mapped into a data pill (crm_account_tier), then written onto the incident record by an Update Record action
It automatically posts to the Teams channel instead of being used elsewhere
It replaces the incident's Priority field
questions.explain: Response mapping turns account_tier into a data pill, which a later Update Record step writes onto the incident.

questions.q: How many custom Script steps does the finished flow in this lab contain?
options: Zero — the Teams half uses a spoke action and the CRM half uses a configured REST step, no custom script
Exactly one, for the Teams integration
Exactly one, for the CRM integration
Two, one for each integration
questions.explain: Both integrations are done through configuration — a spoke action and a REST step — with no custom Script step anywhere in the flow.
